input.question: Which educational institution did Lung Kwang Pan attend?

documents.text: As Dr. Sophia Patel pored over the dusty archives of the university's library, she stumbled upon a faded photograph that caught her attention. It was an old group shot of the Wayne State University's Physics Club, circa 1995. Amidst the sea of unfamiliar faces, one name stood out: Lung Kwang Pan. Sophia's eyes widened as she recognized the name from her research on cutting-edge materials science. The same Lung Kwang Pan, renowned for his groundbreaking work on nanomaterials, had walked the very same campus she now called home. Sophia's curiosity got the better of her, and she began to dig deeper. She tracked down an old professor, Dr. Henry Lee, who had taught at Wayne State during the mid-90s. Over a cup of coffee in the faculty lounge, Dr. Lee regaled Sophia with stories of Lung's time at the university. "He was a quiet, unassuming student," Dr. Lee recalled, "but his intellect was undeniable. He would often stay behind after lectures, peppering me with questions that would leave even the most seasoned professors scratching their heads." As Sophia listened, she imagined Lung Kwang Pan, a young man with an insatiable thirst for knowledge, pouring over textbooks in the very same library where she now sat. She pictured him strolling along the Detroit River, the city's industrial landscape a stark contrast to the futuristic materials he would one day create. Dr. Lee continued, "I remember when Lung presented his thesis on quantum dots. The entire department was abuzz with excitement. We knew we were witnessing something special." Sophia's eyes sparkled with excitement as she scribbled furious notes, her mind racing with the implications of Lung's work. As the sun dipped below the Detroit skyline, Sophia closed her laptop, her thoughts still lingering on the enigmatic Lung Kwang Pan. She felt a sense of pride knowing that the university she called home had played a part in shaping the brilliant mind of a pioneer in his field.
